pull.title: bench: fix `InputType` ODR violation
pull.body:
Introduced in #36475:
```bash
/ci_container_base/src/bench/bip352.cpp:22:12: error: type ‘InputType’ violates the C++ One Definition Rule [-Werror=odr]
   22 | enum class InputType {
      |            ^
/ci_container_base/src/bench/sign_transaction.cpp:24:12: note: an enum with different value name is defined in another translation unit
   24 | enum class InputType {
      |            ^
/ci_container_base/src/bench/bip352.cpp:23:5: note: name ‘P2PKH’ differs from name ‘P2WPKH’ defined in another translation unit
   23 |     P2PKH,           // legacy pubkey-hash
      |     ^
/ci_container_base/src/bench/sign_transaction.cpp:25:5: note: mismatching definition
   25 |     P2WPKH, // segwitv0, witness-pubkey-hash (ECDSA signature)
      |     ^
```

There's a commit here that adds a CI config, using GCC and LTO, which uses `-Wodr`. The existing LTO config uses Clang, and I'm not sure about adding LTO to any existing job. However I do think we should be catching ODR violations in CI.

```
maybe in a new commit: Should this be enabled globally in CI like:

```
ci/test/03_test_script.sh:98:BITCOIN_CONFIG_ALL=(-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$BASE_OUTDIR" -Werror=dev)
.github/ci-test-each-commit-exec.py:41:        "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON",
.github/ci-windows.py:32:        "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON",
.github/ci-windows.py:38:        "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON",

Yea. We could add `-DCMAKE_LINK_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON` to jobs with CMake 4.0+, just need to avoid the macOS cross jobs due to upstream bugs: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35756#issuecomment-7104061664.

Ok, I see. Let's wait for the upstream bug to be fixed first and then just add `-DCMAKE_LINK_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON` globally? IIUC older cmake will just ignore it, which should be fine to avoid the verbosity here of having to place it in every ci task one-by-one?
